candidates.label: notheft (ablation)
candidates.change: Measurement ablation, A and B. A: mov [9769h],ax -> mov [4A17h],ax. B: mov [5D13h],bx -> mov [4A17h],bx. Same length and timing, and both writes are idempotent, so only the two steal writes (and their 2-byte fixed-address arena writes) are removed. 2 bytes differ in each binary.
candidates.groupNotes: Screen: 17 of 50 cohorts changed, W/L 8/5. 2025 -0.0018 (s2025-9 with Registered_Winners -0.111). Strong +0.051 [-0.013,0.115], from sstrong-1 (b01d+e1p4+segment_fault) +0.233, sstrong-2 +0.078, sstrong-5 +0.046. Threat +0.0049, multi -0.0014. Threat htvd5 (8 cohorts x 20 battles per key): RegWinners -0.115 [-0.170,-0.059] 0/7, b01d -0.121 [-0.191,-0.051] 1/6, m050 -0.015 n.s.; ALL -0.083 [-0.125,-0.042]. Threat q97wr (mixAll b01d+e1p4+segfault, 12 cohorts): +0.198 [0.136,0.259] 11/1.

candidates.label: zph (B059, re-tested as the fix for theft self-kill)
candidates.change: B only, zero bytes: zombie_entry mov bp,2000h -> 5C00h and mov bp,3400h -> 7000h. This is B059's binary copied unchanged. Stolen and captured zombies start their phoenix one band higher, so they no longer land on B's still-running startup code.
candidates.groupNotes: Threat ew9rp (mixAll b01d+e1p4+segfault, same cohorts as q97wr): +0.291 [0.219,0.362] 12/0. Base member scores there: w1 0.529, w2 0.057. With zph: w1 0.362, w2 0.515. With notheft: w1 0.423, w2 0.361. General cost was measured earlier by B059/COORD-w2: screen 956md +0.037, confirm pooled +0.0092 [-0.012,+0.030], all gates except pooled-lo pass.

threatFindings.threat: Prevalence of fixed hook cells in realistic pools. Script: agent2/night/scratch/B063/hookscan.mjs (it lists INT 87h with BX=26FFh, the cell, and the straight-line instruction index). [4A17h] is written only by the V6 family (V6/V4/V6Guard). [9769h] is used only by A_HRZ_Registered_Winners (2025): W1 writes [9769h] at instr 3, then W2 at instr 9 and W1 at instr 11 hook EB F9 CC CC -> jmp [9769h], before our B's INT87 at instr 12. [5D13h] is used only by our own lineage (m050, b01d, e1p4, FixedToggle, Synthesis; writes at instr 3-4) and is also written by the V6 family. No 2024 or 2023 team uses any of these cells. Other 2025 hook cells are 8A43h (LowKey, only on a later or zombie path), 1287h (OpcodeHunter2, deep), a data cell (TOM_anonymous), and 4248h/CCCCh (SZR teams, pattern EB FC EB FC, which matches no zom20 Zombie). None is an early competitor for our zombies.
threatFindings.evidence: Static scan of the f2025, l2024, f2024, f2023, counters, peers and refs pools with hookscan.mjs, plus dis86 of each hit. Byte check of the zom20 pack: only E2F281C3 (zom20a) and EB F9 CC CC (zom20b/d) are capturable.
threatFindings.impact: In realistic 2025/2024 fields, only the V6 family can redirect our zombies. A003 measured about +0.015/battle for winning that race (19llx, 5hja6). Registered_Winners is the only realistic team whose zombies we take.

threatFindings.threat: Value of our own steal writes: A's [9769h] copy steals Registered_Winners' early b/d captures, and B's [5D13h] write steals the m050/b01d lineage's captures.
threatFindings.evidence: Ablation notheft: screen zv7iz s2025-9 (contains Registered_Winners) -0.111. Threat htvd5: RegWinners -0.115 [-0.170,-0.059] (Registered_Winners' own score 0.10 vs base rises to 0.24 vs notheft), b01d -0.121 [-0.191,-0.051], m050 -0.015 n.s.
threatFindings.impact: About +0.11/battle in cohorts that contain Registered_Winners (it is 1 of 51 2025 teams, so about +0.006 averaged over the 2025 field), and about +0.12 vs a single b01d. Keep both writes.

threatFindings.threat: Theft self-kill. When two 5D13h-lineage teams are present (b01d+e1p4+segment_fault, as in screen cohort sstrong-1), the zombies stolen through our [5D13h] write kill our own B. The stolen zombies enter B's zombie_entry very early and start their phoenix at phase 2000h/3400h, which runs over B's not-yet-finished startup. This matches the B059 mechanism, made much stronger by early theft.
threatFindings.evidence: Threat q97wr (12 cohorts x 20 battles, mixAll b01d+e1p4+segfault): base team 0.586 with B (w2) only 0.057/battle; notheft +0.198 [0.136,0.259] (w2 0.361). Threat ew9rp, same cohorts: zph (theft kept, stolen-zombie phases moved) +0.291 [0.219,0.362] 12/0 (w2 0.515). The screen cohort sstrong-1 gave the same sign (+0.233). The exact kill site was not traced (a trace job cannot use custom cohorts), so the 'lands on startup code' detail is inferred from zph's effect and B059's trace 4sf0x.
threatFindings.impact: Large (-0.2 to -0.3/battle) but only in cohorts with two or more m050-lineage peers. Those exist in the strong and confirmation fields, not in the archived 2025/2024 fields. Fixed by zph at zero bytes.

threatFindings.threat: Why theft helps against a single b01d (+0.12) but hurts against b01d+e1p4 (-0.2): with two thieves the hooks probably happen earlier or the stolen zombies arrive together, before B leaves startup.
threatFindings.evidence: Only the sign difference between htvd5 (b01d with 2 random 2025 teams) and q97wr (b01d+e1p4+segfault) is measured. The role of segment_fault (INT86 bomber that searches FF 18) was not isolated.
threatFindings.impact: Not needed for the fix: zph removes the harm while keeping the theft.

threatFindings.threat: An opponent or a trail overwrites [4A17h] before our zombies read it. Reads happen early: zom20a at about round 11-15 after A's INT87 at instr 10, and b/d after B's INT87 at instr 12 and zombie_entry searches.
threatFindings.evidence: Static: no realistic team writes 4A17h except the V6 family (B053 scan and hookscan.mjs). The read window is the first tens of rounds, so a late bomb or trail cannot redirect zombies that are already captured. Not traced.
threatFindings.impact: Negligible in realistic fields. A purpose-built [4A17h] poisoner is B073's counter task.

threatFindings.threat: The fixed-address steal writes ([5D13h], [9769h]) also act as blind 2-byte arena writes and add per-cohort chaos.
threatFindings.evidence: Screen zv7iz: cohorts without any hook-cell user changed by up to +-0.1 (lead_V6Guard +0.106, sstrong-2 +0.078, s2025-2 +0.033), while 33 of 50 cohorts stayed identical.
threatFindings.impact: Noise only, no systematic effect. Explains part of the screen strong +0.051.

recommendation: Do not promote notheft. It is a measurement ablation: it loses -0.115 vs Registered_Winners (realistic 2025 team) and -0.121 vs b01d, and its screen +0.0078 comes from strong cohorts where stolen zombies kill our own B. Keep both steal writes. In this domain the realistic danger is not others taking our zombies (only the V6 family can, worth about 0.015 per A003). It is the self-kill caused by zombies we steal early: verified, about -0.2 to -0.3/battle in cohorts with two m050-lineage peers. B059's zero-byte zph removes it (+0.291 [0.219,0.362] on that composition). Recommend that zph be part of the next combination candidate (with B054 fix2steal and A003 C1). Promoting zph alone stays the coordinator's call: its confirm pooled gain was +0.0092 n.s.
